# Sirach Chapter 25 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 25 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**25:1** In three things I find beauty, and they stand approved before the LORD and before men: harmony among brothers, love among neighbors, and a husband and wife who are well suited to each other.

**25:2** Three kinds of persons my soul hates, and their way of life disgusts me greatly: a poor man who is arrogant, a rich man who lies, and an old man who commits adultery without understanding.

**25:3** If you did not gather wisdom in your youth, how will you find it in your old age?

**25:4** How fitting is sound judgment in the gray-haired, and wisdom and counsel in those who are honored!

**25:5** How fitting is wisdom in the elderly, and discernment and counsel in men of distinction!

**25:6** Experience is the crown of the elders, and the fear of the LORD is their glory.

**25:7** Nine things I call blessed in my heart, and the tenth I will speak with my tongue: a man who rejoices in his children; a man who lives to see the fall of his enemies;

**25:8** blessed is one who lives with a sensible wife; and one who has not slipped with his tongue; and one who has not served someone inferior to himself;

**25:9** blessed is one who has found prudence; and one who speaks to listening ears;

**25:10** how great is one who has found wisdom! But none is greater than one who fears the LORD.

**25:11** The fear of the LORD surpasses everything; to what can its possessor be compared?

**25:13** Any wound but not a wound of the heart! Any affliction but not the affliction caused by a woman!

**25:14** Any evil but not the evil of those who hate! And any vengeance but not the vengeance of enemies!

**25:15** There is no head more poisonous than the head of a serpent, and there is no wrath more fierce than the wrath of an enemy.

**25:16** I would rather live with a lion and a dragon than dwell with a wicked woman.

**25:17** The wickedness of a woman changes her expression, and darkens her face like a bear's; and like sackcloth her husband presents himself in the midst of his neighbors.

**25:18** Low spirits that turn to sighing, and a sorrowful heart — a wife who does not make her husband happy.

**25:19** Every evil is trivial compared to the evil of a woman; may the lot of sinners fall upon her.

**25:20** Like the climb of a sandy slope under aged feet — so is a garrulous wife to a quiet man.

**25:21** Do not be taken in by a woman's beauty, and do not desire a woman for her good looks.

**25:22** Anger and shamelessness and great disgrace — when a wife supports her husband.

**25:23** A downcast heart, a sorrowful face, and a wound of the heart — an evil wife. Sagging hands and weakened knees — the wife who does not make her husband happy.

**25:24** From a woman came the beginning of sin, and because of her we all die.

**25:25** Do not give water an outlet, and do not give a wicked woman free rein.

**25:26** If she does not walk by your hand, cut her off from your flesh.
